note: Editorial heuristics for #4138 and #4140, based on the November voice-quality catalogue. Not authorship evidence. Sequence and campaign rules supplement local clauses.

rules.fix: State the positive claim; retain a negated alternative when it corrects a stated belief.

rules.message: A clause ends with a negated alternative.
rules.fix: Keep the useful claim; retain the alternative only when the reader needs the correction.
Name the action, or explain why the alternative was a real option.
State the positive claim, retaining negation when it corrects a misconception.

rules.pattern: (?:^|[.!?]\s+|\n)\s*(?:why (?:it|this|that) (?:matters|helps)|why you should care|what (?:changed|this means(?: for you)?|that means|you get)|the (?:bug|takeaway|point|lesson|catch|upshot|real (?:question|point|story))|bottom line|the short version)\s*:|\b(?:(?:which|that) is the (?:part|thing|bit|point|half) (?:i'd|i would) (?:keep|say|add)(?: too)?|(?:that|this) is the (?:other|real|whole|hard) (?:half|part|point|story|thing))\b
rules.message: A label or aside announces significance.
rules.fix: Explain the circumstance and consequence together; deleting only the label is insufficient.

rules.pattern: \b(?:here'?s the (?:thing|deal|kicker|catch|twist)|here'?s why|let'?s (?:dive|dig|jump) (?:in|into)|let'?s (?:be|get) (?:honest|real|clear)|without further ado|buckle up|picture this|spoiler alert|let me explain)\b|\bfull stop\.
\b(?:what do you think|agree|thoughts|am i wrong|what'?s your take)\?|\b(?:drop a comment|comment below|tag someone who|let me know (?:in the comments|what you think))\b
rules.fix: Ask a concrete question with something to answer, or end with the information.

structuralRules.trigger: Adjacent sentences share the first two tokens and aligned predicates; exactly one polarity flip or listed antonym supplies a real contrast. Different verbs with a negated opener are insufficient.
structuralRules.fix: Combine the useful claim; retain deliberate parallelism with a reason.

structuralRules.trigger: Paragraph-final explicit moral/lesson opener of 3–10 words; allow quoted scenario names inside authored prose but exclude numbers, identifiers, code and wholly quoted statements. Generic closers are not detected.
structuralRules.fix: End on the last useful fact or support the claim.

structuralRules.trigger: Setup of 4–12 words ending in a withheld complement, then a sentence-final punchline of 2–10 words. Also detect a withheld defect followed by an if-clause and a short consequence (at most 16 words after the colon). Frequency never triggers a finding. Exclude lists/definitions, digits/citations and protected material.
structuralRules.fix: State the subject and consequence directly.

structuralRules.trigger: At least four consecutive statements with 1–4 words in one prose paragraph; questions break runs and identical-sentence-only runs are excluded. Also detect a short consequence, a one-word repair and a final explicit moral; the consequence may follow a conditional comma.
structuralRules.fix: Join fragments to explain the reason or result.

structuralRules.trigger: At least six words repeated within an explicit campaign; case and punctuation are ignored, numbers are retained.
structuralRules.fix: Write each channel from its relevant facts.

structuralRules.trigger: An eight-word run inside one sentence shared by at least three distinct documents; overlapping runs merge, affected sentences receive one phrase finding, repeated sentences are excluded.
structuralRules.fix: Rewrite the shared run for the reader and channel.

structuralRules.trigger: First or last three words of the first or last prose sentence shared by three distinct documents, including a content word; numbers and versions normalize to num.
structuralRules.fix: Lead or close with the useful change for this channel.
